meta.title: Malondo Privacy Policy
meta.desc: Malondo has no sign-up. This page states exactly what leaves your device and what stays on it.
title: Malondo Privacy Policy
lead.1: Malondo has no sign-up. We do not ask for your name, email or a password. What you write and what you measure stay on this device and never reach our server — we do not have one. Firebase creates a single anonymous ID with no name so that requests can be counted per person against a daily limit (section 1).
lead.2: That said, at the moment a sentence is written, the situation you typed is sent to Google. Not storing and not sending are different promises, so this document states the difference plainly.
lead.3: This policy is available in 한국어, English, 日本語 and Español. The Korean text is the original; if a translation differs in meaning, the Korean text governs.
s1.a.h: When a sentence is written — Google Gemini
s1.a.1: When suggestions are written, the relationship, conversation goal, word temperature, the situation or draft you typed, your tone settings (sentence length, formality, expressions to avoid) and the language you chose are sent through Firebase AI Logic to the Google Gemini API. The voice reference in the Tone tab (Default · Male · Female) is not sent.
s1.a.received: If you choose Reply to a message in step four, the message you pasted (what the other person sent you) is sent the same way. The same goes for text you hand over with “Find a reply” in the Android share sheet. The message goes out once, at the moment the suggestions are written; it is not stored on your device, and we do not use it to judge what kind of person the sender is.
s1.a.2: When you receive a letter in Unwind first, the story you wrote, the tone you chose, the temperature and length of the reply, and the person involved (if you chose one) go the same way.
s1.a.3: If you use Change with AI (Change just this one with AI), the chosen suggestion and the direction of the change are also sent to Google Gemini. Drafts and change requests are not saved on the device automatically.
s1.a.4: An anonymous user ID that identifies this installation goes along with the request. It is a random name created by Firebase Authentication's anonymous sign-in, made without a name, email or phone number, and it cannot say who you are. It has exactly one use: counting requests per person against a daily limit. Tapping Delete everything removes this ID and takes a new name.
s1.a.5: When Today's sentence is fetched on Home, only the date is sent; the two words for relationship and goal are sent only when the example that fills an empty field is not in the store bundled with the app. In neither case does anything you wrote leave the device.
s1.a.6: We do not store any of this. Once a response is on screen, nothing remains except the sentences you chose to keep. Google's handling follows the Google Privacy Policy.
s1.b.h: When an ad is shown — Google AdMob
s1.b.1: When you choose to watch an ad, and when an ad is fetched in advance, the advertising identifier, device information and approximate location are sent to Google AdMob.
s1.b.2: The situation you typed and the relationship you chose are never sent to the ad side. Where it is required, such as in Europe, ad consent (UMP) is asked for first, and you can change your choice at any time in the app (drawer → Data and privacy).
s1.c.h: When the app crashes — Firebase Crashlytics
s1.c.1: If the app terminates unexpectedly, where the crash happened, the device model, and the operating-system and app version are sent to Firebase Crashlytics. It is used only to find out what broke.
s1.c.2: Nothing you wrote and nothing you received is included. You can turn it off in the app (drawer → Data and privacy → Report crashes). Once off, nothing is sent from that moment on, and it stays off when the app is reopened.
s1.d.h: When it checks for a new version — our website
s1.d.1: From Malondo 1.0.2 onwards. At launch the app only fetches one version table from our website (chunystory.github.io/version.json). Deciding whether the current version can still be used happens on the device, and no value is sent, not even the app version.
s1.d.2: However, an access record (IP address and time) from fetching the file may remain on GitHub's servers, which host this site. We cannot see those records, and no analytics tool is attached to this page.
s1.e.1: Recordings and loudness — never transmitted in any form
s1.e.4: Look-backs — only the relationship, goal, temperature and the answer you chose yourself
s1.e.5: Per-person records — only the date, the person, the name of the temperature you chose and the ℃ measured while reading words meant for that person, kept on the device as a single line
s1.e.6: Anything written in Letting go — nothing is generated on that screen, so it is never transmitted anywhere and never written to a file on the device
s2.1: Measuring the temperature of your words needs microphone permission. Your device asks the first time you record.
s2.2: Your voice never leaves the device. Loudness and frequency analysis happen entirely on it, and all that remains per take is one temperature in ℃ and a timestamp. Audio, loudness samples and frequency values are not stored in any form.
s2.3: The recording file is created temporarily so that you can listen to your own voice once on the result screen, and it is deleted the moment you leave that screen.
s3.1: The following is stored in a single file in the app's documents directory (malondo_state.json).
s3.r1.b: The sentences you chose to keep
s3.r2.b: Sentence length · formality · expressions to avoid · whether tone learning is allowed · voice reference (Default · Male · Female — used only on the device, to set the usual pitch range when measuring word temperature)
s3.r3.b: Relationship · conversation goal · word temperature. They are pre-filled next time. The situation you typed is not here
s3.r4.b: One temperature in ℃ and a timestamp per take. Up to the last 200
s3.r5.b: One line per day, folding together what you measured and the temperature you chose when receiving a letter
s3.r6.b: How many suggestions and letters you received that day. Read by the month panel on Home
s3.r7.b: The relationship, goal and temperature you marked as actually sent, and the answer you chose the next day. No situation text and no suggestion text. Unanswered look-backs are kept for 7 days, answered ones for a year
s3.r8.b: Date · person · the name of the temperature you chose, plus the sum and count of the ℃ measured while reading words meant for that person. Kept as a separate line so that "who and how many times" does not shrink after look-backs are cleared. No situation text and none of the sentences you read
s3.r9.b: How you felt that day and the temperature. Values you chose yourself
s3.r10.b: The date you used Letting go and how many times that day. Shown as a dot on the calendar. What you wrote is not kept
s3.r11.b: How often suggestions were requested, copied and kept, and satisfaction. No sentence text is included
s3.r12.b: Only while you allow it — the number of sentences you edited yourself, the total character count, and how many were formal. Turning it off deletes them
s3.r13.b: The one example sentence received today. It is not used once the date passes
s3.r14.b: How many suggestions and letters you received today. It returns to 0 when the day changes
s3.r15.b: Appearance · language · temperature unit · reading type · reminder time · quiet mode · calendar layers · the crash-report switch
s3.r16.b: One random name for this installation. It points to neither a person nor a device and is never transmitted anywhere
s3.2: The situation you typed, the suggestions you received, the story you shared and its reply are not stored. Look-backs keep no original text either.
s3.3: The anonymous user ID lives not in this file but in the device's Firebase authentication storage. The values the home-screen widget reads (temperature and this month's squares) sit in one more layer, the app's shared storage on the device; with quiet mode on, only the temperature remains.
s3.4: This file is excluded from automatic backup (Google Drive) and device-to-device transfer on Android, and from iCloud backup on iOS. To move to a new device, use the export in section 6.
s4.1: You can turn on one reminder a day (off by default). Scheduling and display happen entirely on the device, passing through neither our server nor a push service. Notification text contains no relationship and no situation.
s5.1: Malondo is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 14.
s6.1: Values on the device stay until you delete them. Unanswered look-backs are deleted automatically after 7 days and answered ones after a year. We retain nothing.
s6.2: You can delete everything at any time:
s6.li.1: In the app — drawer → Data and privacy → Delete everything
s6.li.2: Deleting the app removes the values on the device with it
s6.3: Delete everything removes kept sentences, measurements, look-backs, per-person records, days you let go, tone settings and the installation name, clears the home-screen widget, and deletes the anonymous user ID and takes a new name. Four things remain — today's count (which returns to 0 when the day changes), the quiet-mode switch, the crash-report switch, and the language and temperature unit you chose — and the app's confirmation dialog says why.
s6.4: Since there is no sign-up, there is no account to close. Deleting the app removes the values on the device, and all that remains on a server is one empty anonymous ID that holds no personal information.
s6.5: For moving to a new device there is an export (drawer → Data and privacy). It produces a single file that you move yourself, and we never receive that file.
s7.r1.b: The situation you typed and your tone settings · the message you pasted · the language you chose · the anonymous user ID · crash information
s7.r2.b: Advertising identifier · device information · approximate location
s7.r3.b: Receives nothing — only an access record remains when the version table is served
s7.1: We do not otherwise share or sell personal information.
s8.1: When signs of self-harm, violence or threats are detected, guidance and helpline numbers come before any suggestion. That judgement is made on the device first, and nothing is sent outside before you pass the safety notice.
s8.2: Malondo is not a medical or counselling service and does not replace help from a professional.
s9.1: When this policy changes, we update the effective date on this page, and important changes are announced inside the app.
s9.2: All four language versions are updated on the same day. Where a translation has not caught up, the Korean text governs.
s10.1: For questions about privacy, please write to us.
